title: C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models
venue: NeurIPS 2023 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extended_summary:
This paper introduces C-EVAL, a Chinese evaluation suite for foundation models and large language models. The central problem addressed is that existing benchmarks are mostly English-centric and do not adequately measure advanced knowledge and reasoning in Chinese-language contexts, especially for Chinese users and Chinese educational or professional content.

C-EVAL is built from 13,948 multiple-choice questions spanning 52 subjects across four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional. The benchmark is designed to reduce data contamination by sourcing many questions from mock exams and publicly available documents rather than official national exam papers, and it includes a validation/test split plus a small development set with explanations for few-shot chain-of-thought prompting. The paper also introduces C-EVAL HARD, a subset of eight especially difficult subjects focused on advanced mathematics, physics, and chemistry.

The paper evaluates 11 accessible LLMs, including GPT-4, ChatGPT, Claude, GLM-130B, ChatGLM-6B, LLaMA-65B, Chinese-LLaMA, Chinese-Alpaca, Bloomz-mt, and MOSS. Results show GPT-4 performs best overall, but even it leaves substantial room for improvement; many Chinese-oriented models perform relatively better on Chinese social science and humanities subjects than on STEM. The authors conclude that C-EVAL and C-EVAL HARD fill an important gap for Chinese benchmark evaluation and reveal that advanced reasoning remains difficult for current models.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a benchmark paper for evaluating foundation models, not an intervention study in education. It does not test an educational technology with learners, so there is no causal or correlational evidence about educational outcomes to rate for efficacy.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper’s contribution is infrastructural: a Chinese LLM benchmark (C-EVAL) for model evaluation. It has no direct demonstrated impact on K-12 learners, classrooms, or educational outcomes.
